page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.2xlarge is a burstable compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server features 4 physical cores provisioned into 8 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, paired with 32.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU). Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AVX-512, AES cryptography, and FMA extensions, backed by a 35 MB L3 cache. It operates with a burstable CPU allocation model, provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and contains no local storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate clear performance trade-offs inherent to its burstable profile. Single-core performance falls into lower tiers, recording 870.1 on stress-ng and 884.0 on Geekbench single-core tests. Multi-core throughput achieves average performance tiers across benchmarks, posting a multi-core stress-ng score of 8341.23, a Geekbench multi-core score of 4473.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 9221.03. Application benchmarks show static web serving throughput of 6.57 GB/sec and Redis SET operations reaching 8.5 million operations per second.

The burstable architecture offers high memory density relative to core count at an economical resource profile, making it a viable configuration for variable or light workloads. However, sustained full-core utilization will encounter CPU credit constraints, limiting its efficacy for prolonged heavy compute. Recommended workload applications include general-purpose web serving, microservices, non-continuous batch processing, and low-concurrency database caching.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.2xlarge is a burstable instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY CPU running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading across 4 physical cores, it includes AVX-512 extensions, a 35 MB L3 cache, 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no local storage. Benchmark data reflects low single-core performance alongside average multi-core results, such as a stress-ng multi-core score of 8341.23 and 8.5 million Redis SET operations per second. Due to its burstable CPU allocation model, performance is optimized for intermittent load spikes rather than continuous maximum compute usage. The instance provides strong memory allocation per core, rendering it suitable for web application hosting, build environments, and moderate caching workloads.
